findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||, wrongly denying team admins
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, i.e. the caller must be BOTH an admin and an owner of the booking's team. A user who is a team admin but not the team owner (a common role) is denied with FORBIDDEN when adding guests to team bookings, even though the intent is clearly to allow either role. Should be `||`.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate email checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: The blacklist is lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`), but `uniqueGuests` filters with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so any guest email with uppercase letters (e.g. "User@Spam.com") bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entirely. Similarly `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` is an exact-case compare, so the same attendee can be added twice under different casing, producing duplicate attendees and duplicate emails. Both comparisons should compare lowercased emails.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials/user instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the requesting user. When the requester is an attendee or a team admin (not the booking organizer), the calendar attendee update runs with the caller's calendar credentials, not the organizer's — the update to the organizer's calendar event will fail or, worse, act on the wrong account. The EventManager should be constructed from `booking.user` (which was already fetched with its credentials).

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event type metadata
findings.body: Every other email-sending function in email-manager.ts (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, etc.) checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` so event types that disabled standard emails don't send them. The new `sendAddGuestsEmails` accepts no `eventTypeMetadata` and sends organizer and attendee emails unconditionally, breaking the 'disable standard emails' contract for this notification.

findings.title: Email send errors swallowed without logging the error object
findings.body: The catch block around `sendAddGuestsEmails` only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err`, so failures are undiagnosable in production. Additionally, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 is not wrapped in any error handling — if it throws, the attendees have already been persisted to the DB (line 92) and the mutation rejects while the guests are actually added, leaving DB and calendars out of sync with a confusing error shown to the user.

findings.title: Guests stored with empty name and no validation of booking status
findings.body: New guests are created with `name: ""`, so attendee lists and emails render blank names for these guests (e.g. `to: `${this.attendee.name} <${...}>`" produces `" <a@b.com>"`). Also, the handler does not check `booking.status`, so guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, mutating data and sending 'guests added' emails for events that no longer exist.

findings.title: Stale validation error state when reopening the dialog
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is only reset on the Cancel button click. If the user submits invalid emails (error shown), then closes the dialog via the X / overlay (Dialog onOpenChange) and reopens it, the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error is still displayed even though the input was reset on success or still holds the old values otherwise. Validation state should reset when the dialog opens/closes or when the input changes.

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests endpoint
findings.body: The PR adds a new mutation with non-trivial authorization rules (organizer / attendee / team admin), dedup and blacklist filtering, and email side effects, but no unit or e2e tests are added for any of this — particularly the currently-broken team-admin authorization (`&&` instead of `||`), which a test would have caught.
